dohas.title: Garib namo namo Satpurush koon...
dohas.fullText:
Garib namo namo Satpurush koon, namaskar guru kinh hi.
Sur nar munijan sadhva, santon sarbas dinh hin || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Salutation again and again; complete surrender
The eternal Supreme Truth; the imperishable Supreme Being
Have bowed to the Guru; obeisance to the True Master (Satguru)
Gods, humans, and sages/seers
Saints and holy ones; those on the path of Truth
Have surrendered everything; offered all that one has

dohas.saralarth: Beginning his discourse, Garibdas Ji says — I bow again and again to that eternal Satpurush, the Supreme Being, and I have offered my reverence to my Satguru. To the gods, to humankind, to the sages and seers, to the saints, and to the entire community of holy ones, I have surrendered my everything.
dohas.gahraBhav: In this opening couplet, Garibdas Ji presents the very foundation of spiritual practice — surrender. "Namo namo" carries the sense of continuous, unbroken obeisance, not a one-time gesture. Bowing to the Satpurush and bowing to the Guru are two facets of one and the same consciousness. Offering one's all to everyone reflects the selflessness of the devotee.

dohas.title: Satguru Sahab sant sab...
dohas.fullText:
Satguru Sahab sant sab, dandautam pranam.
Aage peechhe madhya hue, natan koon jaaun kurban || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The true Master; the Supreme Lord God
Prostration; full-body (sashtang) salutation
Past, future, and present — all three times
The humble ones; meek devotees
Devoted; offered up; given in sacrifice

dohas.saralarth: Prostrate salutations to the Satguru, to the Sahab (Lord), and to all the saints. To every devotee who has come before, who will come after, and who is here now — to all those humble souls I offer myself in devotion.
dohas.gahraBhav: In this couplet Garibdas Ji's surrender deepens further. Dandautam pranam — obeisance offered with the whole body, with the ego completely effaced. Remembering the saints of all three times shows that the tradition of devotion is eternal, and that to flow within this stream is itself liberation.

dohas.title: Nirakar nirvisham...
dohas.fullText:
Nirakar nirvisham, kaal jaal bhay bhanjanam.
Nirlepam nij nirgunam, akal anoop besunn dhunn || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Formless; the Supreme Reality without shape
Free of disparity; even-minded and flawless
Destroyer of the snare of Death (Kaal) and of fear
Untainted; untouched by illusion (Maya)
Beyond parts and attributes; indivisible consciousness
Incomparable; one to whom there is no likeness
The unstruck melody that lies beyond the void (Shunya)

dohas.saralarth: That Supreme Being is formless, free of all disparity, the destroyer of the snare of Death and of fear. He is untouched by illusion, self-existent, beyond the gunas, indivisible, incomparable, and is himself the unstruck melody that lies beyond the void.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet glorifies the Supreme through negative attributes (neti-neti, "not this, not this"). "Kaal jaal bhay bhanjanam" — the one who breaks the bondage of death is the true Supreme Being. "Besunn dhunn" points to that state of the unstruck sound (anahad naad) which is heard at the highest stage of meditation.

dohas.title: Soham surati samapatam...
dohas.fullText:
Soham surati samapatam, sakal samana nirati lai.
Ujal hirambar hardamam, be-pravah athah hai, vaar paar nahin madhyatam || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: "That I am" — the realization of "I am Brahman" (Aham Brahmasmi)
The merging of consciousness (surati) into the Supreme
Continuously absorbed, holding all creation within
Luminous sky; the pure sky of consciousness
Every moment; continuously; always
Beyond all flow; of unfathomable depth
No beginning, no end, no middle — limitless

dohas.saralarth: To merge into the surati of "Soham" and, gathering all creation within, to remain continuously absorbed in the Supreme — this is the true practice. That Supreme Reality is present every moment like a luminous sky of consciousness; it is beyond all flow, unfathomably deep, and without beginning, end, or middle.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet is a supreme description of non-dual (Advaita) realization. "Soham" — "I am That" — when this knowledge descends into the surati, the seeker's ego dissolves. "Vaar paar nahin madhyatam" — by negating the Supreme across all three dimensions, its infinitude is expressed.

dohas.title: Garib jo sumirat siddhi hoi...
dohas.fullText:
Garib jo sumirat siddhi hoi, Gananayak Galtana.
Karo anugrah soi, paaras pad pravana || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: By remembering; upon doing remembrance (sumiran)
Attainment is achieved; the work is fulfilled
Lord of the ganas — Lord Ganesha
Galta — the renowned shrine of Ganesha in Rajasthan
Grace; blessing
Feet like the philosopher's stone (paaras), which turn iron to gold

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — may that Gananayak Ganesha, by whose remembrance attainment is achieved and who is enshrined at the shrine of Galta, bestow his grace. Meditation upon his philosopher's-stone-like feet alone makes the soul worthy of the supreme state.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet is an auspicious invocation to Ganesha. "Paaras pad" — just as the philosopher's stone turns iron to gold, the touch of Ganesha's feet refines the seeker's soul. It is a humble petition of devotion.

dohas.title: Aadi Ganesh manaaun...
dohas.fullText:
Aadi Ganesh manaaun, gan nayak devan deva.
Charan kamal lyau laaun, aadi ant karahun seva || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Ganesha, worshipped since the beginning of time; the first to be revered
To propitiate; to please; to worship
Leader of the ganas, god of gods
Lotus-like feet; the sacred feet
To fix; to fix my attention and meditation
May I keep serving from beginning to end

dohas.saralarth: I propitiate Aadi Ganesh, who is the leader of the ganas and the god of gods. I fix my meditation upon his lotus-like feet and will keep serving him from beginning to end.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet is the essence of the praise of Ganesha. "Aadi ant karahun seva" conveys that devotion is not momentary but a lifelong practice. Ganesha is the remover of obstacles, and through his worship all hindrances on the seeker's path are dissolved.

dohas.title: Param shuddhi sangeetam...
dohas.fullText:
Param shuddhi sangeetam, riddhi siddhi data soi.
Avgat gunah ateetam, Satpurush nirmohi || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Supreme purity and music — the holiness of the divine sound
Giver of prosperity and attainments (riddhi-siddhi)
All-knowing; the one who knows everything
Beyond the gunas; transcending the three qualities
Free of attachment; without delusion

dohas.saralarth: That Supreme Being is the source of supreme purity and divine music — he alone is the giver of prosperity and attainment. He is all-knowing, beyond the gunas, and is the Satpurush who is wholly free of attachment.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet beautifully harmonizes both the positive and the negative aspects of the Supreme. "Param shuddhi sangeetam" — the Supreme is himself music, he is purity itself. And at the same time "nirmohi" — being bound to none, he can belong to all.

dohas.title: Jagdamba Jagdeesham...
dohas.fullText:
Jagdamba Jagdeesham, mangal roop Murari.
Tan man arpun sheesham, bhakti mukti bhandari || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Mother of the world; the primordial Shakti
Lord of the world; master of creation
The auspicious form; Vishnu, slayer of the demon Mur
To offer one's head; complete surrender
Keeper of the treasure of both devotion and liberation

dohas.saralarth: To Jagdamba, mother of the world, and to Jagdeesh, lord of the world — the auspicious-formed Murari — I offer my body, mind, and head. They are the keepers of the treasure of both devotion and liberation.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet venerates both Shakti and Shiva (Jagdamba and Jagdeesh) together — a symbol of the non-dual vision. "Tan man arpun sheesham" is a threefold surrender that expresses the fullness of devotion. To seek devotion and liberation together reflects the maturity of the devotee.

dohas.title: Sur nar munijan dhyaavain...
dohas.fullText:
Sur nar munijan dhyaavain, Brahma Vishnu Mahesha.
Shesh sahans mukh gaavain, poojain Aadi Ganesha || 9 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Gods, humans, and sages
Meditate upon; worship
The trinity — creator, preserver, and destroyer
The thousand mouths of Sheshnaag, the cosmic serpent
Ganesha, worshipped since the beginning of time

dohas.saralarth: Gods, humans, and sages — all meditate. Brahma, Vishnu, and Mahesh — all worship. Sheshnaag sings with his thousand mouths — and they all worship Aadi Ganesha.
dohas.gahraBhav: What is striking in this couplet is that even the trinity themselves worship that supreme power (in the form of Ganesha). It shows that all bow before the highest power of the cosmos. "Shesh sahans mukh gaavain" — that glory is so vast that even a thousand mouths cannot fully describe it.

dohas.title: Indra Kuber sarikha...
dohas.fullText:
Indra Kuber sarikha, Varun Dharmaray dhyaavain.
Sumrath jeevan jeeka, man ichchha phal paavain || 10 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The likes of Indra and Kubera — king of the gods and god of wealth
God of water; lord of the waters
Yamraj, god of dharma; the judge of deeds
Meditate upon; worship
The being whose remembrance (sumiran) is powerful and effective
Receive the fruit of the heart's desire

dohas.saralarth: Even great gods like Indra, Kubera, Varun, and Dharmaraj meditate upon that supreme power. The being who does remembrance (sumiran) of that power receives the fruit of the heart's desire.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet shows even the presiding deities as worshippers of that supreme power. The sense conveyed is that for one who remembers the Supreme, all the gods become favourable. The devotee need not beg of anyone else — remembrance of the Supreme alone grants everything.

dohas.title: Tetees koti adhara...
dohas.fullText:
Tetees koti adhara, dhyaavain sahans athasi.
Utrain bhavjal paara, kati hain yam ki phaansi || 11 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Thirty-three crore gods and goddesses
The support; the foundation on which all rest
Eighty-eight thousand — the count of sages and seers
Crossing the ocean of worldly existence; liberation
The noose of Yamraj is cut; freedom from the bondage of death

dohas.saralarth: That Supreme Reality, which is the support of the thirty-three crore gods and which eighty-eight thousand sages meditate upon — by remembering it one crosses the ocean of worldly existence and the noose of Yamraj is cut away.
dohas.gahraBhav: This final couplet concludes the Mangalacharan. "Tetees koti adhara" — that Supreme Being is the support of the entire host of gods. "Yam ki phaansi" — freedom from the cycle of death and rebirth. Thus Garibdas Ji conveys the message that meditation upon that one Supreme Reality is the sole path to liberation from all obstacles, fear, and bondage.

dohas.title: Prapin pralok hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapin pralok hai, jahan adli Satguru saar.
Bhaddhi het sain utre, paaya ham deedar || 1 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The supreme realm; the highest abode of the world beyond
Just; true; the upholder of justice
The Satguru is the very essence — the supreme reality
For the sake of devotion; by reason of bhakti
Sight; vision; divine darshan

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — that supreme realm is utterly wondrous, where the just Satguru is seated in person. For the sake of devotion he descended from that supreme abode, and we received his divine vision.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet tells of the glory of the Guru's descent from the world beyond. The Satguru himself dwells in that supreme abode where there is no fear of Kaal (Death). His coming here is an act of grace upon the devotees.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — alal pankh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, alal pankh ki jaat.
Kaaya maaya na vahan, nahin pind nahin gaat || 2 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Of the kind with 'alakh' (unseen) wings — a formless, divine being
Body and the world of illusion
The physical body
Limb; a part of the body

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — I met such a Satguru who belongs to the kind with unseen (alakh) wings, that is, to the formless Supreme Reality. Where he dwells there is no body and no illusion, neither physical form nor any limb.
dohas.gahraBhav: This describes the divine nature of the Satguru — he is beyond the body. His existence is in that realm which is free of all materiality. To meet such a Guru is exceedingly rare and a matter of great fortune.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — ujal hirambar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, ujal hirambar aanad.
Bhalka gyaan kamaan ka, ghaalat hain sar saandhi || 3 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Luminous sky; the clear sky of knowledge
The very form of bliss; bliss made manifest
Flashing like lightning; swift and piercing
Of the bow of knowledge
Takes aim and strikes at the head — strikes with the arrow of knowledge

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is the very form of bliss, like a luminous sky. Drawing a lightning-swift arrow upon the bow of knowledge, he takes aim at the head of ignorance.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Guru's knowledge strikes its target directly like an arrow — at the very head of ignorance, illusion, and delusion. 'Bhalka gyaan' — this is knowledge that has an instant and certain effect.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — sunn videshi...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, sunn videshi aap.
Rom-rom prakash hai, deenha ajapa jaap || 4 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Dweller of the realm beyond the void; transcending Shunya
Light in every pore; divine radiance throughout the body
The unspoken recitation; name-remembrance that flows of itself with the breath

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is the dweller of the realm beyond even the void. He filled every pore with light and bestowed the divine secret of the ajapa jaap.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Ajapa jaap' is that state in which 'Soham' recites itself within the seeker's incoming and outgoing breath. By the Guru's grace this effortless practice begins. 'Rom-rom prakash' — the state of divine awakening.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — magan kiye mustaak...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, magan kiye mustaak.
Pyaala pyaaya prem ka, gagan mandal gar gaap || 5 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Made me absorbed and longing; rapt and immersed
Made me drink the cup of love; gave the divine nectar of love
The sphere of the inner sky; the divine region of the Sahasrar
Merged deep within; secretly immersed in bliss

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who made me utterly absorbed and rapt in the Supreme. He made me drink the divine cup of love, by which I sank deep into the sphere of the inner sky.
dohas.gahraBhav: The cup of love is that grace of the Guru which lifts the devotee out of the world and immerses him in the Supreme. To merge into the gagan-mandal is the dissolving of consciousness in the Sahasrar chakra.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — sindhu surati ki sain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, sindhu surati ki sain.
Ur antar prakaasiya, ajab sunaaye bain || 6 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The sign and beckoning of the ocean of consciousness (surati)
Light arose within the heart
Spoke wondrous words; uttered an unearthly speech

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who gave the beckoning toward the ocean of surati. By his grace light arose within the heart, and he uttered a wondrous, unearthly speech.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Guru's speech is not ordinary — it is 'ajab bain,' unearthly. Hearing it, light is at once kindled in the heart. 'Surati sindhu' — to show the way to dive into the boundless ocean of consciousness is the work of the Guru.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — surati sindhu ki sail...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ki sail.
Bajra paul pi khol kar, le gaya jheeni gail || 7 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A journey through the ocean of consciousness
A door hard as a thunderbolt; a firmly shut gate
A subtle path; a fine narrow way; the path of the Self

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who took me on a voyage of the ocean of surati. He opened the door that was shut hard as a thunderbolt and led me onto the most subtle path of the Self.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Bajra paul' — the obstructions that block the seeker from reaching the supreme reality. By the Guru's grace these hard doors swing open and 'jheeni gail' — that subtle path which joins the soul to the Supreme — is laid open.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — surati sindhu ke teer...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ke teer.
Sab santan sir taaj hain, Satguru adli Kabir || 8 ||

shabdarth.meaning: On the shore of the ocean of consciousness
The crown upon the head; the foremost of all
The just Kabir; Kabir Sahib, the upholder of Truth

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is seated on the shore of the ocean of surati. He is the crown upon the head of all saints — the just Satguru Kabir Sahib, the upholder of Truth.
dohas.gahraBhav: Here Garibdas Ji directly recognizes the Satguru as Kabir Sahib. 'Sab santan sir taaj' — in the whole tradition of saints, Kabir Sahib is supreme. 'Adli' — he is just; Truth is his very nature.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — surati sindhu ke maanhi...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ke maanhi.
Shabd swaroopi ang hai, pind praan nahin chhaanhi || 9 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Within the ocean of consciousness
A body in the form of Shabd (the Word); the embodied form of divine speech
Not even the shadow of body or breath; beyond all materiality

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who dwells within the ocean of surati. His every limb is of the form of Shabd (the Word) — there is not even the shadow of body or breath.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's body is not physical but 'shabd swaroopi' — he is the embodied form of divine speech. When the seeker descends into the ocean of surati, what he finds there is a pure conscious being, free of body and free of illusion.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — galtaana gulzaar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, galtaana gulzaar.
Vaar paar keemat nahin, nahin halka nahin bhaar || 10 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Galta — a garden brimming with bliss; a flourishing place
Of no measurable price; priceless
Neither light nor heavy; weightless, beyond comparison

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who dwells in a garden of bliss like Galta. His worth is beyond all reckoning — he is neither light nor heavy; he is beyond all comparison.
dohas.gahraBhav: The glory of the Guru cannot be weighed on any scale. 'Nahin halka nahin bhaar' — he is beyond all duality, past every measure. 'Galtaana gulzaar' — to go to him is a journey into bliss.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — surati sindhu ke manjh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ke manjh.
Andron aanand pokh hai, bain sunaaye kunj || 11 ||

shabdarth.meaning: In the midst of the ocean of consciousness; at the centre of consciousness
Bliss nourished from deep within; inner bliss sustained
Spoke words in the bower; gave divine speech in solitude

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who abides at the very centre of the ocean of surati. There, bliss is nourished deep within, and he uttered divine words in the solitude of the bower.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Andron aanand pokh' — this spiritual bliss is not received from outside; it is born and nourished within. 'Kunj mein bain sunaaye' — the Guru's most profound teaching, given in solitude.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — surati sindhu ke naal (peetambar)...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ke naal.
Peetambar taakhi dhayo, baani shabd rarsaal || 12 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Alongside the ocean of consciousness
Wore yellow garments; appeared in divine raiment
Speech and words full of nectar; sweet divine utterance

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who walks alongside the ocean of surati. He wore yellow raiment and uttered the words of a sweet, nectar-filled divine speech.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Peetambar taakhi dhayo' — this form of the Satguru is Vishnu-like. 'Baani shabd rarsaal' — the Guru's speech is not knowledge alone but nectar too; it satisfies the soul.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — surati sindhu ke naal (gavan kiya)...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ke naal.
Gavan kiya parlok se, alal pankh ki chaal || 13 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Came forth from the world beyond; descended from the supreme abode
The gait of the unseen (alakh) wings; the movement of the formless

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who descended from the world beyond, alongside the ocean of surati. His gait is like that of the unseen wings — formless, imperceptible, and boundless.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's coming into this world is of his own free will. He is a dweller of the world beyond and comes here for the deliverance of devotees. 'Alal pankh ki chaal' — there is no burden of body in his movement; he is free, formless consciousness.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — gyaan jog bhaddhi...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, surati sindhu ke naal.
Gyaan jog aur bhaddhi sab, deenhi nazar nihaal || 14 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Knowledge, yoga, and devotion — all three paths
Blessed me with his gracious glance; uplifted me by his gaze

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who, alongside the ocean of surati, bestowed all three — knowledge, yoga, and devotion — together, and uplifted me with his gracious glance.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru does not give just one path — he grants the combined initiation of knowledge, yoga, and devotion. 'Nazar nihaal' — by the Guru's glance alone the seeker's life is transformed.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — beparvah abandh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, beparvah abandh.
Param hans poorn purush, rom-rom ravi chand || 15 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Free of all flow, free of all bondage; limitless
The supreme Hans — the highest adept or divine soul
The complete Being; the wholly perfect Reality
Light like the sun and moon in every pore

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is beyond all flow and all bondage. He is the supreme Hans, the perfect Being — in whose every pore the radiance of sun and moon abides.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Rom-rom ravi chand' — this describes the blazing inner light of the Satguru. Param Hans and Poorn Purush — both epithets declare that he is free of every imperfection.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — zinda Jagdeesh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, hai zinda Jagdeesh.
Sunn videshi mil gaya, chhatra mukut hai sheesh || 16 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The living Lord of the world; the Supreme made manifest
Dweller of the realm beyond the void
A divine canopy and crown upon his head; king of kings

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is the living Jagdeesh — the dweller of the realm beyond the void. Upon his head shine a divine canopy and crown.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Zinda Jagdeesh' — the Satguru is no distant, formless entity; he is living, manifest, and present. 'Chhatra mukut hai sheesh' — his majesty is unearthly; he is the supreme king of kings.

dohas.title: Satguru ke lakshan kahoon — madhure bain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru ke lakshan kahoon, madhure bain vinod.
Chaar bed shat shastra, kah athaara bodh || 17 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Sweet and delightful speech; pleasing words
The four Vedas and the six Shastras
The knowledge of the eighteen Puranas

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji tells the marks of the Satguru — his speech is sweet and delightful. He is complete in the knowledge of the four Vedas, the six Shastras, and the eighteen Puranas.
dohas.gahraBhav: The first mark of the Satguru is sweet speech. One who utters bitter words is no Satguru. He is also a master of all the scriptures — no limit of knowledge can bind him.

dohas.title: Satguru ke lakshan kahoon — achal vihangam...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru ke lakshan kahoon, achal vihangam chaal.
Ham amraapur le gaya, gyaan shabd sar ghaal || 18 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A steady yet bird-free gait; an unwavering movement
The immortal city; the place of liberation; the deathless realm
By loosing the arrow of the Word of knowledge

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji tells the marks of the Satguru — his gait is unwavering yet free as a bird's. By loosing the arrow of the Word of knowledge, he carried us to the immortal city.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Vihangam chaal' — the bird-like motion that soars in the sky, free of worldly bonds. 'Amraapur le gaya' — this is the greatest mark of the Satguru: that he carries the disciple to the immortal state.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — turiya ke teer...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, turiya ke re teer.
Bhagal vidya baani kahain, chhaanai neer aru kheer || 19 ||

shabdarth.meaning: On the shore of the Turiya state; near the fourth state of consciousness
Illusion-shattering knowledge; divine wisdom
Separates milk from water — sifts the essential from the worthless

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is seated on the shore of the Turiya state. He utters the speech of illusion-shattering divine knowledge and, like milk from water, separates the essence from the worthless.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Turiya' — the fourth state of consciousness beyond waking, dream, and deep sleep. The Satguru abides on the shore of that state. 'Neer-kheer' — as the swan separates milk from water, so the Satguru separates truth from falsehood.

dohas.title: Zinda jogi jagat guru — maalik murshad peev...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, zinda jogi jagat guru, maalik murshad peev.
Kaal karam laagai nahin, nahin shanka nahin seev || 20 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The living yogi; the manifest lord of yoga
Murshid — the spiritual master; the beloved Supreme
Untouched by the effect of Death (Kaal) and karma
Neither doubt nor limit

dohas.saralarth: That Satguru is the living yogi, the guru of the world, the master, the murshid, and the beloved Supreme. Neither Death nor karma touches him — for him there is no doubt and no limit.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Zinda jogi' — the yogi who is inwardly awake. 'Kaal karam laagai nahin' — the Satguru is beyond the cycle of karma and Death. 'Nahin shanka nahin seev' — his state is doubtless and boundless.

dohas.title: Zinda jogi jagat guru — dahu deen jhagra...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, zinda jogi jagat guru, maalik murasad peer.
Dahu deen jhagra mara, paaya nahin sharir || 21 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A dispute arose between the two faiths (Hindu and Muslim)
His body was not found; no corpse was seized

dohas.saralarth: That Satguru is the living guru of the world, the master, the murshid, and the pir. The two faiths (Hindu and Muslim) quarrelled over him, yet none could find his body.
dohas.gahraBhav: On Kabir Sahib's passing, both Hindus and Muslims disputed over his remains. But when the shroud was lifted, flowers were found — not a body. This is the proof of his unearthly nature.

dohas.title: Zinda jogi jagat guru — maaya bhalka bhed...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, zinda jogi jagat guru, maalik murshad peer.
Maaya bhalka bhed se, lage gyaan ke teer || 22 ||

shabdarth.meaning: By piercing the illusion of Maya; by tearing through delusion
The arrows of knowledge strike home; knowledge descends straight into the heart

dohas.saralarth: That living guru of the world — master, murshid, and pir — pierces the illusion of Maya and looses the swift arrows of knowledge.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's task is not merely to impart knowledge — he tears away the veil of Maya. As long as the covering of illusion remains, knowledge cannot reach within. 'Gyaan ke teer' — swift, direct, and of certain effect.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — tej punj ke ang...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, tej punj ke ang.
Jhil mil noor jahar hai, roop rekh nahin rang || 23 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A body that is a mass of radiance; a body of light
A shimmering light is manifest; a glimmering radiance
No form, no outline, no colour — formless

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru whose body is a mass of radiance. From him a shimmering light is manifest, yet he has no form, no outline, and no colour.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's divine form is a mass of light — radiance and glow. 'Roop rekh nahin rang' — he is formless, and yet his presence is felt. This divine paradox points to Self-realization.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — tej punj ki loy...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, tej punj ki loy.
Tan man arpoon sheesh koon, honi hoy su hoy || 24 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The flame of the mass of radiance; the blaze of divine light
I offer my head; I bow down
Whatever is to be will be — surrendered to the will of the Supreme

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who is the flame of the mass of radiance. I offer my body, mind, and head — let whatever is to be, be, according to the will of the Supreme.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Honi hoy su hoy' — this is the spirit of total surrender. The devotee's ego dissolves; he says, 'Not my will, but the Guru's will is my will.' This is the maturity of devotion.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — khole bajra kivaar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, khole bajra kivaar.
Agam deep koon le gaya, jahan Brahma darbaar || 25 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Doors hard as a thunderbolt; firmly shut gates
An unreachable light; an inaccessible divine isle
The court of Brahma; the divine court of the Supreme

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who opened the thunderbolt-hard doors and carried me to that unreachable isle of light where the court of the Supreme is held.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Bajra kivaar' — the obstacles that hold a seeker back for years. By the Guru's grace they open in an instant. 'Brahma darbaar' — the place of the Supreme's presence, the final goal of every seeker.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — khole bajra kapaat...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, khole bajra kapaat.
Agam bhoomi koon gam kari, utre aughat ghaat || 26 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Doors firm as a thunderbolt; hard barriers
Made the unreachable land reachable
A difficult, impassable ford; a hard place

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who opened the thunderbolt-hard doors, made the unreachable land reachable, and brought me down the impassable ford.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's work is to make passable what is impassable. 'Aughat ghaat' — that hard crossing which none can descend without a Guru. The Guru's grace is the only means.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — maari gyaasi gain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, maari gyaasi gain.
Rom-rom mein saalti, palak nahin hai chain || 27 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Cast a deep, penetrating gaze
Pierces every pore; stabs to the depths
Not a moment's peace; no instant of rest

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who cast a deep, piercing gaze. That gaze stabs into every pore, and since then there is not a moment's peace.
dohas.gahraBhav: Under the Guru's glance the devotee becomes restless — but this restlessness is the restlessness of spiritual awakening. Whoever is once seen by the Guru's deep gaze can no longer revel in the world.

dohas.title: Satguru bhalka khainch kar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru bhalka khainch kar laaya baan ju ek.
Swaans ubhaare saalta pada kaleje chhek || 28 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Drawing back like lightning; with swift force
A single arrow; one lone shaft
Stings with every drawn breath
Pierced into the heart; lodged deep within the breast

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — the Satguru drew back like lightning and loosed a single arrow. It stings with every breath and lies lodged deep in the heart.
dohas.gahraBhav: Once the Guru's arrow of knowledge lodges in the devotee's heart, it never comes out. This arrow is of love, and of pain too — yet this very pain is awakening.

dohas.title: Satguru maaya baan kas...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru maaya baan kas, khaibar gyaasi khainch.
Bharam karam sab jar gaye, lai kubuddhi sab ainch || 29 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Drawing taut the Maya-piercing arrow; with the arrow that destroys illusion
A deep draw like Khaibar; with great force
All delusion and karma were burnt away
Drew out all wrong thinking; took away the corrupt mind

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — the Satguru drew taut and loosed the Maya-piercing arrow. By it all delusion and karma were burnt away, and all wrong thinking was drawn out and removed.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's arrow of knowledge destroys three things at once — delusion (ignorance), karma (the bondage of accumulated deeds), and wrong thinking (perverse understanding). This is the essence of the practice of liberation.

dohas.title: Satguru aaye daya kari...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru aaye daya kari, aise deen dayaal.
Bandi chhod birad taas ka, jatharaani pratipaal || 30 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Merciful to the lowly; compassionate
Freer of captives; the liberator
Biruda — title, vow, renown
Protector even from the fire of the womb

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru came in his mercy — such is he, compassionate to the lowly. His title is 'Freer of Captives.' He protects the soul even from the fire of the womb.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Bandi chhod' — this is Kabir Sahib's special title. He frees from bondage — of birth and death, of karma, of Maya. 'Jatharaani pratipaal' — even amid the agony of the womb, he is the protector.

dohas.title: Jatharaani sain raakhiya...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, jatharaani sain raakhiya, pyaaya amrit kheer.
Jugan-jugan satsang hai, samajh kutan bepeer || 31 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Protected from the fire of the womb
Nectar-like kheer; the essence of immortality
A satsang-bond across age after age
One who instructs without causing pain; a painless teaching

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — he protected me from the fire of the womb and gave me nectar-kheer to drink. This satsang has continued age after age — understand it in a spirit free of pain.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's bond is not of this birth alone — 'jugan-jugan satsang' — it is a tie across ages. The relationship of Guru and disciple is eternal.

dohas.title: Jooni sankat met hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, jooni sankat met hain, aundhe mukh nahin aay.
Aisa Satguru seiye, jam sain let chhudaay || 32 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The torment of the womb; the agony of birth and death
Comes not head-downward again; is not reborn
Frees one from Yama (Death)

dohas.saralarth: Serve such a Satguru who wipes away the torment of the womb, by whose grace one need not come again head-downward into birth, and who frees one even from Yama.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Aundhe mukh nahin aay' — the infant comes head-downward in the womb, a symbol of suffering. By the Satguru's grace this cycle is broken. This couplet inspires service to the Satguru.

dohas.title: Jam jaura jaasain darain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, jam jaura jaasain darain, dharma raay ke doot.
Chaudah koti na champ heen, sun Satguru ki koot || 33 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Whom the messengers of Death and Kaal fear
The messengers of Dharmaraj (Yamraj)
Not even fourteen crore can overpower
Hear the glory of the Satguru

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — hear the glory of the Satguru! Death and Kaal fear him, the messengers of Dharmaraj fear him, and even fourteen crore messengers of Death cannot overpower him.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru's power is greater than Kaal. Whoever takes refuge in the Satguru has no fear of Yama. 'Chaudah koti na champ heen' — this is no exaggeration; it is a spiritual truth.

dohas.title: Jam jaura jaase darain — dharmaray dharai dheer...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, jam jaura jaase darain, dharma raay dharai dheer.
Aisa Satguru ek hai, adli adal Kabir || 34 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Even Dharmaraj holds his patience; waits in restraint
The just and righteous Kabir Sahib, representative of Truth

dohas.saralarth: Death and Kaal fear him, and even Dharmaraj waits in patient restraint before him — such a Satguru is but one: the just and righteous Kabir Sahib, the upholder of Truth.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet declares the uniqueness of the one Satguru. Kabir Sahib alone is that being who is beyond Kaal, Yama, and Dharmaraj — beyond them all.

dohas.title: Jam jaura jaasain darain — miten karam ke ank...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, jam jaura jaasain darain, miten karam ke ank.
Kaagaj keerai dargah dai, chaudah koti na champ || 35 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The reckoning of deeds; the account of karmic fruit
Tears up the deed-record and submits it to the divine court
Not even fourteen crore messengers of Death can overpower

dohas.saralarth: Death fears him, and by his grace the reckoning of deeds is erased; the karmic record is torn up and submitted to the supreme court — not even fourteen crore can overpower such a devotee.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Kaagaj keerai' — the destruction of the karmic record is a symbol of liberation. When the bondage of karma ends, the fear of Kaal is no more.

dohas.title: Jam jaura jaase darain — miten karam ke lekh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, jam jaura jaase darain, miten karam ke lekh.
Adli adal Kabir hain, kul ke Satguru ek || 36 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The written record of deeds; the script of destiny
The one and only Satguru of all creation

dohas.saralarth: Death fears him, and through him the written record of deeds is erased — the just Kabir Sahib alone is the one and only Satguru of all creation.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Kul ke Satguru ek' — Kabir Sahib belongs not to one tradition alone but is the guru of all creation. His knowledge is universal and timeless.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — pahunchya manjh nidaan...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, pahunchya manjh nidaan.
Nauka naam chadhaay kar, paar kiye parvaan || 37 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Arrived in the very midst; came into the heart of the crisis
Setting one aboard the boat of the Name
Carried across with honour; ferried over, accepted

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who arrived in the very midst of the crisis and, setting me aboard the boat of the Name, carried me across with honour.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Nauka naam' — the Name of the Supreme is that boat which ferries one across the ocean of existence. The Satguru is the one who sets the soul aboard that boat.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — bhau sagar ke maahi...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, bhau sagar ke maahi.
Nauka naam chadhaay kar, le raakhe nij thaahi || 38 ||

shabdarth.meaning: In the midst of the ocean of worldly existence
Took me to and set me in his own abode; revealed the true home

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who came into the midst of the ocean of existence and, setting me aboard the boat of the Name, carried me to his own true abode.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Nij thaahi' — that supreme place which is the soul's original home, whence it came and whither it must return. The Satguru shows the way to that home.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru ham milya — bhau sagar ke beech...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru ham milya, bhau sagar ke beech.
Khevat sab koon khevta, kya uttam kya neech || 39 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Ferries everyone across like a boatman
No distinction of high or low; all are equal

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who, in the midst of the ocean of existence, ferries everyone across like a boatman — with no distinction of high or low, superior or inferior.
dohas.gahraBhav: There is no discrimination in the Satguru's grace — 'kya uttam kya neech.' He holds equal compassion for all. This couplet carries the message of equality.

dohas.title: Chaurasi ki dhaar mein...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, chaurasi ki dhaar mein, bahe jaat hain jeev.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, le prasaaya peev || 40 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The current of the eighty-four lakh life-forms
Souls are being swept along; wandering adrift
The Beloved took one in; the Supreme made one his own

dohas.saralarth: Souls are being swept along in the current of the eighty-four lakh births — and at such a time I met a Satguru who united me with the beloved Supreme.
dohas.gahraBhav: The eighty-four lakh births — a symbol of the soul's wandering. The Satguru brings that wandering to an end. 'Peev' — the beloved Supreme, union with whom is the soul's ultimate goal.

dohas.title: Lakh chaurasi dhaar mein...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, lakh chaurasi dhaar mein, bahe jaat hain hans.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, alakh lakhaaya bans || 41 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The eighty-four lakh life-forms
The souls (hans) are being swept along; wandering
Revealed the unseen Supreme; introduced the supreme lineage

dohas.saralarth: The souls (hans) are being swept along in the current of the eighty-four lakh births — and at such a time I met a Satguru who revealed the unseen Supreme and made known to me that supreme lineage.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Alakh lakhaaya' — to grant the power to perceive what cannot be perceived — this is the Guru's greatest grace.

dohas.title: Maaya ka ras peey kar — phoot gaye do nain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, maaya ka ras peey kar, phoot gaye do nain.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, baas diya sukh chain || 42 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Having drunk the nectar of Maya; drowning in worldly pleasures
Both eyes burst — sight was lost; discernment vanished
Granted an abode of happiness and peace

dohas.saralarth: Having drunk the nectar of Maya, both eyes burst (discernment was lost) — and at such a time I met a Satguru who granted me an abode of happiness and peace.
dohas.gahraBhav: The nectar of Maya tastes sweet but destroys sight (discernment). When discernment is gone, the way cannot be seen. The Satguru restores that very lost sight.

dohas.title: Maaya ka ras peey kar — ho gaye daamaadol...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, maaya ka ras peey kar, ho gaye daamaadol.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, gyaan jog diya khol || 43 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Unsteady, confused, tottering
Unveiled and gave the secret of knowledge and yoga

dohas.saralarth: Having drunk the nectar of Maya I became tottering and unsteady — and at such a time I met a Satguru who unveiled for me the deep secret of knowledge and yoga.
dohas.gahraBhav: Maya makes a person unsteady; knowledge gives stability. The Guru unveils the secret that no amount of self-study can yield.

dohas.title: Maaya ka ras peey kar — ho gaye bhoot khais...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, maaya ka ras peey kar, ho gaye bhoot khais.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, bhaddhi dai bakshish || 44 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Became degraded like a ghost; fallen and corrupted
Bestowed the gift of devotion; granted bhakti as a boon

dohas.saralarth: Having drunk the nectar of Maya I became degraded like a ghost — and at such a time I met a Satguru who bestowed upon me the gift of devotion.
dohas.gahraBhav: Maya leads to ruin, the Guru to upliftment. 'Bhaddhi bakshish' — devotion is not had for free; it is a special gift of the Guru's grace.

dohas.title: Maaya ka ras peey kar — phoot gaye pat chaar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, maaya ka ras peey kar, phoot gaye pat chaar.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, loyan shankh ughaar || 45 ||

shabdarth.meaning: All four shutters burst open — the four directions closed in
Opened the eyes like a conch — granted divine sight

dohas.saralarth: Having drunk the nectar of Maya the four shutters burst (all directions closed in) — and at such a time I met a Satguru who opened my eyes, conch-bright, and granted divine sight.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Loyan shankh ughaar' — the conch is white and pure. The Satguru opened those eyes that grant a clear and holy vision.

dohas.title: Maaya ka ras peey kar — doob gaye dahaan deen...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, maaya ka ras peey kar, doob gaye dahaan deen.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, gyaan jog praveen || 46 ||

shabdarth.meaning: On both sides, in both faiths; everywhere
Skilled in knowledge and yoga; adept

dohas.saralarth: Having drunk the nectar of Maya I drowned on both sides — and at such a time I met a Satguru adept in both knowledge and yoga.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Dahaan deen' — to drown on both sides means the snare of Maya in both world and religion. Only a Satguru adept in knowledge and yoga can free one from both snares.

dohas.title: Maaya ka ras peey kar — gaye shat dal gaarat...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, maaya ka ras peey kar, gaye shat dal gaarat gor.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, pragat liye bahor || 47 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The six chakras fell into a pit; the six centres became blocked
Brought back by awakening them; revived and restored

dohas.saralarth: Having drunk the nectar of Maya the six chakras fell into a pit (became blocked) — and at such a time I met a Satguru who revealed and revived them once more.
dohas.gahraBhav: Maya blocks the six chakras. The Satguru re-awakens them. This is a subtle pointer to the practice of Kundalini.

dohas.title: Satguru koon kya deejiye...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru koon kya deejiye, dene koon kuchh naahin.
Sanman koon saata kiya, seoo bhent chadhaahi || 48 ||

shabdarth.meaning: There is nothing to give; nothing of one's own
Struck a bargain with the mind; gave the mind in exchange
Offer your very self as the gift

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — what is there to give the Satguru when one has nothing to give! Strike a bargain with the mind, and offer your very self as the gift.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru has no need of material offerings. What he wants is the surrender of mind and soul. 'Sanman koon saata' — to hand over the mind to the Guru is the greatest offering of all.

dohas.title: Sir saate ki bhaddhi hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sir saate ki bhaddhi hai, aur kuchh naahin baat.
Sir ke saate paaiye, avgat alakh anaath || 49 ||

shabdarth.meaning: In exchange for the head; through complete surrender
This is devotion; this is the root of bhakti
Imperceptible, unseen, and dependent on none — three names of the Supreme

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — devotion is had only in exchange for the head; there is no other matter. Only by giving the head (the ego) is the imperceptible, unseen, master-less Supreme attained.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Sir saate' — the complete dissolution of the ego. So long as the 'I' remains, the Supreme is not found. 'Avgat alakh anaath' — three aspects of the Supreme: imperceptible, invisible, and dependent on none.

dohas.title: Sheesh tumhaara jaayega — kar Satguru koon daan...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sheesh tumhaara jaayega, kar Satguru koon daan.
Mera meri chhaad de, yohi goi maidaan || 50 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Your head is destined to go; death is certain
Give it in charity to the Satguru; surrender it
Let go of possessiveness and ego
This is the real battlefield; this is the true field

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — this head is destined to go anyway, so give it in charity to the Satguru. Let go of 'mine' and 'my' (possessiveness) — this very thing is the real battlefield.
dohas.gahraBhav: The renunciation of ego and possessiveness is the true battle — 'yohi goi maidaan.' This is no outer war but an inner struggle, where the 'I' must be defeated.

dohas.title: Sheesh tumhaara jaayega — kar Satguru ki bhent...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sheesh tumhaara jaayega, kar Satguru ki bhent.
Naam nirantar leejiye, jam ki lagain na phent || 51 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Offer it to the Satguru; surrender the head
Do remembrance of the Name unceasingly
So the noose of Yama may not catch you; Death cannot seize you

dohas.saralarth: This head is destined to go — so offer it to the Satguru. Keep doing remembrance of the Name unceasingly, so that the noose of Yama may never catch you.
dohas.gahraBhav: Even while accepting the inevitability of death, there is a way to remain free of fear — remembrance of the Name and surrender. This couplet states the truth of life and death and its spiritual resolution.

dohas.title: Sahib se Satguru bhaye...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sahib se Satguru bhaye, Satguru se bhaye saadh.
Ye teenon ang ek hain, gati kachu agam agaadh || 52 ||

shabdarth.meaning: From the Sahib (the Supreme) the Satguru came forth
From the Satguru the saints came to be
Their way is unfathomable and beyond reach

dohas.saralarth: From the Sahib (the Supreme) the Satguru came forth, and from the Satguru the saints came to be — these three are one and the same. Their way is beyond reach and unfathomable.
dohas.gahraBhav: The triad of Supreme — Satguru — saint is one. This threesome is indivisible and of one essence. To know this truth is itself Self-knowledge.

dohas.title: Sahib se Satguru bhaye — dhar-dhar bhesh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sahib se Satguru bhaye, Satguru se bhaye sant.
Dhar-dhar bhesh vishaal ang, khelen aadi aur ant || 53 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Assuming various guises, in many forms
Play their divine sport from beginning to end

dohas.saralarth: From the Sahib the Satguru came forth, and from the Satguru the saints — assuming various guises, they play their divine sport from beginning to end.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Dhar-dhar bhesh' — the Supreme's play unfolds in endless forms. Sometimes as a Hindu, sometimes as a Muslim, sometimes as a yogi — yet within, it is one and the same consciousness.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru seiye — beg utaare paar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru seiye, beg utaare paar.
Chaurasi bhram metahin, aava gavan nivaar || 54 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Carries one across swiftly
Erases the delusion of the eighty-four lakh births
Ends the cycle of coming and going (birth and death)

dohas.saralarth: Serve such a Satguru who carries one across swiftly, erases the delusion of the eighty-four lakh births, and ends the cycle of birth and death.
dohas.gahraBhav: Three tasks — to carry across, to erase delusion, to end birth and death. This is the threefold grace of the Satguru. One who can grant all three is the true Satguru.

dohas.title: Andhe goonge guru ghane...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, andhe goonge guru ghane, langde lobhi laakh.
Sahib sain parche nahin, kaav banaavain saakh || 55 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Abundant are the blind and mute (ignorant) gurus
Lakhs who are lame (crippled in knowledge) and greedy
Have no acquaintance with the Supreme
Like crows, they fabricate testimony; offer false praise

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji warns — there is an abundance of ignorant, mute, lame, and greedy gurus. Those who have no acquaintance with the Supreme fabricate false testimony, like cawing crows.
dohas.gahraBhav: Recognizing the true Satguru is essential. Amid the abundance of false gurus, the true one is hard to discern. To go to one who has no direct acquaintance with the Supreme is futile.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru seiye — shabd samaana hoy...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru seiye, shabd samaana hoy.
Bhau sagar mein doobten, paar langhaavain soy || 56 ||

shabdarth.meaning: One absorbed in the Shabd; merged in the divine Word
Those drowning in the ocean of existence
He alone carries them across

dohas.saralarth: Serve such a Satguru who is absorbed in the Shabd (the divine Word) and who carries across those drowning in the ocean of existence.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Shabd samaana' — only that Satguru who has himself merged into the Shabd-Brahma can carry others to that state.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru seiye — Soham sindhu milaap...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru seiye, Soham sindhu milaap.
Turiya madhya aasan karain, metain teenon taap || 57 ||

shabdarth.meaning: One who unites you within the ocean of Soham
Abides established in the Turiya state
Erases the three afflictions (physical, divine, and spiritual)

dohas.saralarth: Serve such a Satguru who unites you within the ocean of Soham, who abides in the Turiya state, and who erases all three afflictions.
dohas.gahraBhav: The three afflictions are the three kinds of worldly suffering. The Satguru frees one from all three. 'Turiya madhya aasan' — he is ever established in the fourth state.

dohas.title: Turiya par puriya mahal — shabd vigyaana nes...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, turiya par puriya mahal, paar Brahma ka desh.
Aisa Satguru seiye, shabd vigyaana nes || 58 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The palace beyond even Turiya; the fifth state
The realm of Parabrahma; the supreme abode
Versed in the science of the Shabd; a knower of Shabd-Brahma

dohas.saralarth: Beyond Turiya lies the palace of Puriya, which is the realm of Parabrahma. Serve such a Satguru who is versed in the science of the Shabd.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Turiya par puriya' — beyond even Turiya there is a further state, called the fifth or Puriya. The true Satguru is a knower of that state.

dohas.title: Turiya par puriya mahal — hans karain nihkaam...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, turiya par puriya mahal, paar Brahma ka dhaam.
Aisa Satguru seiye, hans karain nihkaam || 59 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The abode of Parabrahma; the supreme dwelling
Make the soul desireless; free it of all craving

dohas.saralarth: Beyond Turiya lies the palace of Puriya — the abode of Parabrahma. Serve such a Satguru who makes the soul desireless.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Nihkaam' — the desireless state. When all the soul's desires are extinguished, it rests in the supreme abode. The Satguru grants that state.

dohas.title: Turiya par puriya mahal — hans pathaavain mokh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, turiya par puriya mahal, paar Brahma ka lok.
Aisa Satguru seiye, hans pathaavain mokh || 60 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The realm of Parabrahma; the realm of liberation
Send the soul into liberation

dohas.saralarth: Above Turiya lies the palace of Puriya — the realm of Parabrahma. Serve such a Satguru who delivers the soul into liberation.
dohas.gahraBhav: The supreme service of the Satguru is this: that he carries the disciple's soul to liberation. 'Hans pathaavain mokh' — this is the Guru's highest duty and highest grace.

dohas.title: Turiya par puriya mahal — raakhe sang sameep...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, turiya par puriya mahal, paar Brahma ka dweep.
Aisa Satguru seiye, raakhe sang sameep || 61 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The isle of Parabrahma; the island of supreme consciousness
Keeps one near and beside him; holds one close

dohas.saralarth: Above Turiya lies the palace of Puriya — the isle of Parabrahma. Serve such a Satguru who keeps you ever near and beside him.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Raakhe sang sameep' — an important quality of the Satguru is that he never leaves the disciple alone. His presence remains ever-constant on the spiritual journey.

dohas.title: Gagan mandal gaadi jahan...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, gagan mandal gaadi jahan, paar Brahma asthaan.
Sunn shikhar ke mahal mein, hans karain vishraam || 62 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A throne in the sphere of the sky; a seat in the celestial region
The seat of Parabrahma; the supreme abode
In the palace of the void-summit; the highest consciousness

dohas.saralarth: In the sphere of the sky is the throne of Parabrahma. In the palace of the void-summit the soul (hans) takes its rest.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Sunn shikhar ke mahal' — the state even above the Sahasrar, where the soul finds supreme rest. To reach there is itself liberation.

dohas.title: Satguru poorn Brahma hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru poorn Brahma hain, Satguru aap alekh.
Satguru ramta Raam hain, yaamein meen na mekh || 63 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Is the complete Brahma; the perfect Supreme
Is himself indescribable; beyond all account
The all-pervading Ram; present everywhere
Without flaw or fault; absolute truth

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is the complete Brahma, the Satguru is himself indescribable, the Satguru is the all-pervading Ram — in this there is no flaw and no fault.
dohas.gahraBhav: There is no difference between the Satguru and the Supreme — 'meen na mekh.' This is not mere sentiment but a spiritual truth. One who sees the Supreme in the Satguru is the true disciple.

dohas.title: Satguru aadi anaadi hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru aadi anaadi hain, Satguru madhya hain mool.
Satguru koon sijda karoon, ek palak nahin bhool || 64 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Was at the beginning and is from beginningless time
Is also the root in the middle; the foundation throughout
Sijda — I make prostrate obeisance
I do not forget for even a moment; ever-remembering

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is both the beginning and the beginningless, and the root even in the middle. I bow to him in prostration — never forgetting him for even a moment.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru is timeless — present at the beginning, from beginningless time, and in the middle too. 'Ek palak nahin bhool' — the devotee's unceasing remembrance and surrender.

dohas.title: Pattan ghaat lakhaaiyan — asht kamal dal chhed (1)...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, pattan ghaat lakhaaiyan, agam bhoomi ka bhed.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, asht kamal dal chhed || 65 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The wharf of the supreme city; a divine landing-place
Revealed the secret of the unreachable land
Pierced the eight-petalled lotus; awakened the lotus of eight petals

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who showed me the wharf of the supreme city, revealed the secret of the unreachable land, and pierced the eight-petalled lotus.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Asht kamal dal chhed' — the awakening of the eight-petalled heart-lotus. This symbolizes the activation of the heart-chakra, which comes by the Satguru's grace.

dohas.title: Pattan ghaat lakhaaiyan — asht kamal dal sev (2)...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, pattan ghaat lakhaaiyan, agam bhoomi ka bhev.
Aisa Satguru ham milya, asht kamal dal sev || 66 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Another form of 'bhed' — secret, hidden knowledge
The practice and worship of the eight-petalled lotus

dohas.saralarth: I met such a Satguru who showed me the supreme wharf, revealed the hidden secret of the unreachable land, and showed the path of practice upon the eight-petalled lotus.
dohas.gahraBhav: The previous couplet had 'chhed' (piercing); here it is 'sev' (practice). Piercing and practice are sequential stages — first the lotus is pierced, then its practice is undertaken.

dohas.title: Prapattan ki peeth mein — sir saate sauda...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapattan ki peeth mein, Satguru le gaya mohi.
Sir saate sauda hua, agli pichhli khohi || 67 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The seat of the supreme city; the throne of the highest realm
A bargain struck in exchange for the head — the ego given, the Supreme gained
All searching, before and after; complete self-inquiry

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru carried me to the seat of the supreme city. There a bargain was struck in exchange for the head, and all the secrets, before and after, were laid open.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Sir saate sauda' — the exchange in which knowledge is gained by giving up the ego. Whoever consents to this bargain has all the secrets revealed to him.

dohas.title: Prapattan ki peeth mein — heere maanik bikain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapattan ki peeth mein, Satguru le gaya saath.
Jahan heere maanik bikain, paaras laagya haath || 68 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Where diamonds and rubies are sold; priceless gems are found
The philosopher's stone came to hand; the supreme gem was obtained

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru took me along to the seat of the supreme city. There diamonds and rubies are sold, and the philosopher's stone came into my hand.
dohas.gahraBhav: The 'diamonds and rubies' found in the supreme abode are the gems of knowledge, devotion, dispassion, and liberation. 'Paaras laagya haath' — the Satguru himself is the philosopher's stone who turns an iron-like soul into gold.

dohas.title: Prapattan ki peeth mein — saudaagar son saat...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapattan ki peeth mein, hai Satguru ki haat.
Jahan heere maanik bikain, saudaagar son saat || 69 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Satguru's shop; the marketplace of knowledge
A deal with the merchant; a transaction with the trader

dohas.saralarth: In the seat of the supreme city stands the Satguru's shop. There diamonds and rubies are sold, and one strikes a deal with the merchant of knowledge.
dohas.gahraBhav: The Satguru runs a 'haat' — a marketplace of knowledge. Whoever comes may take it away. The price is only one: the renunciation of ego.

dohas.title: Prapattan ki peeth mein — sauda hai nij saar...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapattan ki peeth mein, sauda hai nij saar.
Ham koon Satguru le gaya, aughat ghaat utaar || 70 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The bargain there is with one's own supreme essence
Brought one down the difficult ford; carried across the hard crossing

dohas.saralarth: In the seat of the supreme city, the bargain is with one's own supreme essence. The Satguru took me there and brought me down the impassable ford.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Nij saar' — the essential reality of one's own soul. On reaching the supreme city one recognizes one's own soul — this is the greatest bargain of all.

dohas.title: Prapattan ki peeth mein — prem pyaale khoob...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapattan ki peeth mein, prem pyaale khoob.
Jahan ham Satguru le gaya, matvaala mehboob || 71 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Cups of love in abundance; the nectar of love in full
The Beloved rapt in love; intoxicated with love

dohas.saralarth: In the seat of the supreme city where the Satguru took me — there were cups of love in abundance, and I met the Beloved (the Supreme) rapt in love.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Matvaala mehboob' — that intoxication of love in which awareness of self is lost. This is the highest state of Sufi devotion, where the devotee and the Supreme become one.

dohas.title: Prapattan ki peeth mein — matvaale mastaan...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, prapattan ki peeth mein, matvaale mastaan.
Ham koon Satguru le gaya, amraapur asthaan || 72 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Immersed in rapture; lost in the intoxication of love
The immortal city; the place of liberation

dohas.saralarth: In the seat of the supreme city are the rapt and the intoxicated. The Satguru took me there, to the seat of the immortal city.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Amraapur' — the supreme abode where there is no birth or death. The Satguru showed the seeker the way to that city where he may rest forever.

dohas.title: Bank naal ke antare — maan sarovar hans...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, bank naal ke antare, triveni ke teer.
Maan sarovar hans hain, baani kokil keer || 73 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The curved channel — a part of the Sushumna nadi
On the bank of the confluence of the three nadis
Mansarovar — the abode of the swan; the lake of the soul
Sweet speech like the cuckoo and the parrot

dohas.saralarth: Within the curved channel, on the bank of the Triveni confluence, the swans abide in Mansarovar, where sweet speech like cuckoo and parrot resounds.
dohas.gahraBhav: This describes the inner journey of the subtle body. 'Triveni' — the confluence of Ida, Pingala, and Sushumna. There the swan (the soul) rests and the divine sound is heard.

dohas.title: Bank naal ke antare — chuvai amiras kheer...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, bank naal ke antare, triveni ke teer.
Jahan ham Satguru le gaya, chuvai amiras kheer || 74 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Nectar and milk-essence drip down; drops of ambrosia fall

dohas.saralarth: Within the curved channel, on the bank of the Triveni where the Satguru took me — there the stream of nectar and divine essence drips down.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Amiras kheer' — the divine nectar that drips from the Sahasrar when the Kundalini awakens. This is not a physical but a spiritual experience.

dohas.title: Bank naal ke antare — bandi chhod Kabir...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, bank naal ke antare, triveni ke teer.
Jahan ham Satguru le gaya, bandi chhod Kabir || 75 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Kabir Sahib, the freer of captives

dohas.saralarth: Within the curved channel, on the bank of the Triveni, the Satguru took me to where Kabir Sahib, the freer of captives, abides.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet reveals that in the depths of the curved channel is the presence of Kabir Sahib. 'Bandi chhod' — he frees one from all bonds.

dohas.title: Bhanvar gufa mein baith kar — sauda rokam rok...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, bhanvar gufa mein baith kar, ami mahaaras jokh.
Aisa Satguru mil gaya, sauda rokam rok || 76 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Bhanvar Gufa — the inner cave above the Sahasrar
Weighing and testing the great nectar
A cash bargain; a settled, on-the-spot deal

dohas.saralarth: Seated in the Bhanvar Gufa, testing the great nectar — I met such a Satguru with whom a cash bargain was struck.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Bhanvar gufa' — an exceedingly deep spiritual state. 'Rokam rok' — when the Satguru is met, the change is instant and direct, with no delay.

dohas.title: Bhanvar gufa mein baith kar — bajra paul dai khol...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, bhanvar gufa mein baith kar, ami mahaaras tol.
Aisa Satguru mil gaya, bajra paul dai khol || 77 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Weighing and measuring the great nectar
Opened the thunderbolt-door

dohas.saralarth: Seated in the Bhanvar Gufa, weighing the great nectar — I met such a Satguru who opened the thunderbolt-door.
dohas.gahraBhav: In the Bhanvar Gufa is the thunderbolt-door — the final barrier. By the Satguru's grace even this opens, and the seeker enters into the supreme truth.

dohas.title: Bhanvar gufa mein baith kar — le gaya ham pralok...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, bhanvar gufa mein baith kar, ami mahaaras jokh.
Aisa Satguru mil gaya, le gaya ham pralok || 78 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Carried me to the world beyond; brought me to the supreme realm

dohas.saralarth: Seated in the Bhanvar Gufa, testing the great nectar — I met such a Satguru who carried me to the world beyond (the supreme realm).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Pralok le gaya' — the experience of the world beyond within this very life. When the Bhanvar Gufa opens, the seeker experiences the supreme abode even while in the body.

dohas.title: Pind brahmand sain agam hain — dekhya agam agaadh...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, pind brahmand sain agam hain, nyaari sindhu samaadh.
Aisa Satguru mil gaya, dekhya agam agaadh || 79 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Beyond the body and the cosmos; unreachable
A distinct ocean-samadhi; a unique meditative state
Beheld the unreachable and unfathomable

dohas.saralarth: That which is beyond the body and the cosmos, where a unique ocean-samadhi is held — I met such a Satguru through whom I beheld the unreachable, unfathomable reality.
dohas.gahraBhav: By the Satguru's grace, that is beheld which no practice can reveal. 'Agam agaadh' — the supreme truth beyond the bounds of body and cosmos.

dohas.title: Pind brahmand sain agam hain — diya akhai prasaad...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, pind brahmand sain agam hain, nyaari sindhu samaadh.
Aisa Satguru mil gaya, diya akhai prasaad || 80 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Imperishable grace; a gift that never runs out

dohas.saralarth: That which is beyond the body and the cosmos — I met such a Satguru who bestowed an imperishable grace.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Akhai prasaad' — the gift that never ends. The Guru's gift — knowledge, devotion, grace — is imperishable. Once received, it serves through life after life.

dohas.title: Aughat ghaati utre...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aughat ghaati utre, Satguru ke updesh.
Poorn pad prakaasiya, gyaan jog pravesh || 81 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Descended the impassable valley; crossed the hard path
The perfect state was revealed; the supreme state shone forth
Gained entry into knowledge and yoga

dohas.saralarth: By the Satguru's teaching the impassable valley was descended. The perfect state was revealed, and entry into knowledge and yoga was gained.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Aughat ghaati' — the hard path that cannot be crossed without a Guru. The teaching is the very means that carries one across this valley.

dohas.title: Sunn sarovar hans man...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sunn sarovar hans man, nhaaya Satguru bhed.
Surati nirati parcha bhaya, asht kamal dal chhed || 82 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The lake of the void; the ocean of the Self
Bathed in the Satguru's secret; immersed in the mystery
Surati and nirati became acquainted; the two were joined

dohas.saralarth: In the lake of the void the mind bathed, immersed in the Satguru's secret. Surati and nirati became acquainted, and the eight-petalled lotus was pierced.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Surati-nirati' — the consciousness that ascends and the awareness that descends. When the two become acquainted, the state of samadhi arrives.

dohas.title: Sunn besunn sain agam hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sunn besunn sain agam hai, pind brahmand sain nyaar.
Shabd samaana shabd mein, avgat vaar na paar || 83 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Beyond even the void and the great void
Distinct from body and cosmos
Word merged into the Word; dissolved into the supreme Shabd
The imperceptible Supreme has neither shore nor far bank

dohas.saralarth: The supreme Reality is beyond even the void and the great void, distinct from body and cosmos. Word is merged into the Word, and the imperceptible Supreme has neither shore nor far bank.
dohas.gahraBhav: The indescribability of the Supreme — it is beyond all bounds. 'Shabd samaana shabd mein' — all is dissolved into the supreme Sound.

dohas.title: Satguru koon kurban jaaun...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru koon kurban jaaun, ajab lakhaaya des.
Paar Brahma pravaan hai, niraalambh nij nes || 84 ||

shabdarth.meaning: I am devoted; I offer myself in sacrifice
Showed a wondrous land; revealed an unearthly realm
The supportless, self-established state; self-existent and self-sufficient

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — I am devoted to the Satguru who showed me a wondrous land. Parabrahma is proven there, supportless and self-established in its own being.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Ajab lakhaaya des' — that land seen not with the eyes but with the soul. 'Niraalambh' — needing no support, the self-existent Supreme.

dohas.title: Satguru Soham naam de...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru Soham naam de, guj beeraj vistaar.
Bin Soham seejhe nahin, mool mantra nij saar || 85 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Guru's seed (mantra) expanded; the spreading of the seed-mantra
Without Soham nothing is accomplished
This is the root-mantra and one's own essence

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru gave the Soham Name, and the Guru's seed-mantra spread within. Without Soham nothing is accomplished — this is the root-mantra and one's own essence.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Soham' — 'I am That.' This is not merely a mantra but the realization of the Self. When the Satguru bestows it, an awakening stirs in the seeker's soul.

dohas.title: Soham Soham dhun lagai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Soham Soham dhun lagai, durad band dil maahin.
Satguru parda khol heen, paraalok le jaahin || 86 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The melody of Soham resounds; the unstruck sound plays
The bond of pain within the heart; the heart's lock shut
The Satguru lifts the veil; removes the covering

dohas.saralarth: The melody of Soham resounds, the bond of pain locked within the heart — the Satguru lifts that veil and carries one to the world beyond.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Durad band' — the lock of the heart, shut by ignorance. The Satguru opens it. 'Paraalok le jaahin' — the journey to the world beyond happens within this very life.

dohas.title: Soham jaap ajaap hai — chadhe mahal sukh sej...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Soham jaap ajaap hai, bin rasna hoe dhunn.
Chadhe mahal sukh sej par, jahan paap nahin punn || 87 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The recitation that needs no reciting; the jaap that goes on of itself
The melody sounds without the tongue; resounds without being uttered
Upon the bed of bliss; in supreme ease
Where there is no distinction of sin and merit; beyond duality

dohas.saralarth: Soham is the unspoken recitation — the melody sounds without the tongue. The seeker ascends to the bed of bliss, where there is no distinction of sin and merit.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Ajaap' — that highest state of practice where no reciter remains; the recitation goes on of itself. 'Paap nahin punn' — reaching the state beyond duality.

dohas.title: Soham jaap ajaap hai — Satguru deep sameep...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Soham jaap ajaap hai, bin rasna hoe dhunn.
Satguru deep sameep hai, nahin basti nahin sunn || 88 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The Satguru's lamp is near; the light is close at hand
Neither town nor void; beyond them both

dohas.saralarth: Soham is the unspoken recitation, the melody sounding without the tongue. The Satguru's lamp is near — where there is neither town nor void, beyond them both.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Nahin basti nahin sunn' — the Supreme is neither in the town nor in the wilderness. It is beyond both, within. The Satguru's lamp gives the light of that very place.

dohas.title: Sunn basti sain rahit hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, sunn basti sain rahit hai, mool mantra man maahin.
Jahan ham Satguru le gaya, agam bhoomi sat thaahin || 89 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Free of both void and town
The root-mantra abides within the mind
The seat of Truth in the unreachable land

dohas.saralarth: Free of both void and town — the root-mantra abides within the mind. The Satguru took me where, in the unreachable land, lies the seat of Truth.
dohas.gahraBhav: The seat of Truth is neither in the town nor in the wilderness, neither in noise nor in silence. It is within. The Satguru shows the path to that inner place.

dohas.title: Mool mantra nij naam hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, mool mantra nij naam hai, soorat sindhu ke teer.
Gaibi baani aras mein, sur nar dharain na dheer || 90 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The root-mantra is one's own Name (the Name of the Supreme)
On the shore of the ocean of consciousness
The unseen divine speech in the highest sky (Arsh)
Gods and humans cannot hold their composure; are spellbound

dohas.saralarth: The root-mantra is the very Name of the Supreme, on the shore of the ocean of consciousness. In the highest sky resounds the unseen divine speech, hearing which even gods and humans cannot keep their composure.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Gaibi baani' — the unstruck speech that none has uttered yet which is heard. This is the highest experience of the anahad naad.

dohas.title: Ajab nagar mein le gaya...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, ajab nagar mein le gaya, ham koon Satguru aan.
Jhilke bimb agaadh gati, soote chaadar taan || 91 ||

shabdarth.meaning: A wondrous city; an unearthly place
Reflections shimmer with unfathomable motion
As though asleep with the sheet drawn over — in supreme rest

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru took me into that wondrous city where reflections shimmer with unfathomable motion, and there is a supreme peace like sleeping with a sheet drawn over.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Ajab nagar' — the supreme state to which the seeker is taken. 'Chaadar taan soote' — a carefree, burdenless, utterly restful state.

dohas.title: Agam anaahad deep hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, agam anaahad deep hai, agam anaahad lok.
Agam anaahad gavan hai, agam anaahad mokh || 92 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The isle of the unreachable, unstruck sound
The journey of the unreachable, unstruck sound
The unreachable, unstruck sound is itself liberation

dohas.saralarth: There is the isle of the unreachable, unstruck sound; the realm of the unreachable, unstruck sound; the journey of the unreachable, unstruck sound; and the unreachable, unstruck sound is itself liberation.
dohas.gahraBhav: This couplet gives the fourfold glory of the 'unreachable unstruck' — isle, realm, journey, and liberation. All is in that one reality. This is the essence of the whole practice, in brief.

dohas.title: Satguru paaras roop hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru paaras roop hain, hamri loha jaat.
Palak beech kanchan karain, paltain pindru gaat || 93 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Is like the philosopher's stone
We are of the kind of iron — hard and tarnished
Turns one to gold in the blink of an eye
Transforms the body; remakes it utterly

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is like the philosopher's stone; we are of the kind of iron. In the blink of an eye he turns one to gold and transforms the whole body.
dohas.gahraBhav: The philosopher's-stone-and-iron metaphor is the supreme example of the Guru-disciple bond. As the stone transforms iron, so the Satguru transforms the seeker. 'Palak beech' — the change can be instantaneous.

dohas.title: Ham to loha kathin hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, ham to loha kathin hain, Satguru bane luhaar.
Jugan-jugan ke morche, tod ghade ghansaar || 94 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The blacksmith, who forges hard metal
The rust of age after age; the crust of old sins
Breaking and forging it, refined it thoroughly

dohas.saralarth: Garibdas Ji says — we are hard iron, and the Satguru became the blacksmith. Breaking and forging away the rust of age after age, he refined us.
dohas.gahraBhav: The blacksmith — here a special form of the Guru. He heats hard iron in the fire and forges it with the hammer into something useful. This is the very process of spiritual practice.

dohas.title: Ham pasuva jan jeev hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, ham pasuva jan jeev hain, Satguru jaat bhirang.
Murde sain zinda karain, palat dharat hain ang || 95 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Beings dull as beasts; ignorant creatures
Of the bee-kind — one who turns the sucked flower into honey (transforms)
Brings the death-like back to life
Transforms one's every limb; remakes the being

dohas.saralarth: We are beings dull as beasts; the Satguru is of the bee-kind. He brings the death-like back to life and transforms one's every limb.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Jaat bhirang' — the bee, which makes even an insect into its own kind. So the Satguru makes even a beast-like soul divine.

dohas.title: Satguru sikleegar bane...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru sikleegar bane, yauh tan tega deh.
Jugan-jugan ke morche, khovain bharam sandeh || 96 ||

shabdarth.meaning: The sword-polisher, who sharpens the blade
A body like a sword; a keen-edged form
Erases delusion and doubt

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru became the sword-polisher — this body is the sword. He wears away the rust of age after age (delusion and doubt).
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Sikleegar' — one who sharpens the edge. The Guru sharpens the seeker's intellect and discernment. The rust is the delusion and doubt that have caked on across ages.

dohas.title: Satguru koon deepak hain...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, Satguru koon deepak hain, hamri tunka deh.
Swaati seep ka mel hai, chand chakora neh || 97 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Is the lamp; a pillar of light
A tiny body; a body slight as a straw
The union of the Swati raindrop and the oyster
The love of the moon and the chakor bird

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru is the lamp; we are a tiny body. Our union is like that of the Swati raindrop and the oyster, like the love of the moon and the chakor bird.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Swaati-seep' — if a drop of rain falls into an oyster during the Swati constellation, it becomes a pearl. Just so, a single drop of the Guru's grace turns a worthy disciple into a pearl.

dohas.title: Aisa Satguru seiye — beg udhaarai hans...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, aisa Satguru seiye, beg udhaarai hans.
Bhau sagar aavai nahin, jaura kaal vidhvans || 98 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Swiftly delivers the soul
One need not come again into the ocean of existence
Destroyer of Kaal (Death) and Yama

dohas.saralarth: Serve such a Satguru who swiftly delivers the soul, by whose grace one need not return to the ocean of existence, and who is the destroyer of Death.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Jaura kaal vidhvans' — the Satguru is the destroyer of Kaal. Whoever takes his refuge has no fear of Death. 'Bhau sagar aavai nahin' — no more rebirth.

dohas.title: Pattan nagri ghar karai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, pattan nagri ghar karai, gagan mandal gainaar.
Alal pankh jyoon sancharai, Satguru adham udhaar || 99 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Makes his home in the supreme city
A mass of light in the sphere of the sky
Moves about like the unseen (alakh) wings
Delivers even the most fallen

dohas.saralarth: The Satguru makes his home in the supreme city and shines in the sphere of the sky. Moving like the unseen wings, he delivers even the most fallen.
dohas.gahraBhav: 'Adham udhaar' — the greatest mark of the Satguru is that he delivers even the most fallen and lowly. None is excluded from his grace.

dohas.title: Alal pankh anuraag hai...
dohas.fullText:
Garib, alal pankh anuraag hai, sunn mandal rahai theer.
Daas Garib udhaariya, Satguru mile Kabir || 100 ||

shabdarth.meaning: Love for the unseen (alakh) wings; devotion to the formless
Remains steady in the sphere of the void
The servant Garib was delivered

dohas.saralarth: There is love for the unseen, and he remains steady in the sphere of the void. The servant Garib was delivered — for the Satguru Kabir was found.
dohas.gahraBhav: This is the closing couplet of the Ang. 'Satguru mile Kabir' — this is the proclamation of Garibdas Ji's supreme realization. All the practice, all the journey, all the struggle — all of it was for this one union.
